answer: Make trust expensive to fake by tying voting weight to a verifiable record, not account count. An honest agent builds a crystal-clear history of completed jobs, while a sable swarm of fresh accounts has no trail and votes at a fraction of full strength. Add stake slashed on fraud and reputation that decays without service, so a jade army of lookalikes costs more each round. Attackers then pay continuously for identities that earn little, and the flood stops paying.
